verses.zh: （大卫的诗，交与伶长。）耶和华啊，我投靠你；求你使我永不羞愧；凭你的公义搭救我！
verses.en: For the music director, a psalm of David.In you, O Lord, I have taken shelter.Never let me be humiliated.Vindicate me by rescuing me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 31. The psalmist confidently asks the Lord to protect him. Enemies threaten him and even his friends have abandoned him, but he looks to the Lord for vindication. In vv. 19-24, which were apparently written after the Lord answered the prayer of vv. 1-18, the psalmist thanks the Lord for delivering him.

verses.zh: 求你侧耳而听，快快救我！作我坚固的磐石，拯救我的保障！
verses.en: Listen to me.[NOTE:1] Quickly deliver me.Be my protector and refuge,[NOTE:2] a stronghold where I can be safe.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “in your vindication rescue me.”
Heb “turn toward me your ear.”
Heb “become for me a rocky summit of refuge.”

verses.zh: 因为你是我的岩石，我的山寨；所以，求你为你名的缘故引导我，指点我。
verses.en: For you are my high ridge[NOTE:1] and my stronghold;for the sake of your own reputation[NOTE:2] you lead me and guide me.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “a house of strongholds to deliver me.”
The metaphor of the high ridge pictures God as a rocky, relatively inaccessible summit, where one would be able to find protection from enemies. See 1 Sam 23:25, 28.
Heb “name.” The Hebrew term שֵׁם (shem, “name”) refers here to the Lord’s reputation. (The English term “name” is often used the same way.)

verses.zh: 求你救我脱离人为我暗设的网罗，因为你是我的保障。
verses.en: You will free me[NOTE:1] from the net they hid for me,for you are my place of refuge.
notes: The present translation assumes that the imperfect verbal forms are generalizing, “you lead me and guide me.” Other options are to take them as an expression of confidence about the future, “you will lead me and guide me” (cf. NASB), or as expressing a prayer, “lead me and guide me” (cf. NEB, NIV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 我将我的灵魂交在你手里；耶和华诚实的　神啊，你救赎了我。
verses.en: Into your hand I entrust my life;[NOTE:1] you will rescue[NOTE:2] me, O Lord, the faithful God.
notes: Heb “bring me out.” The translation assumes that the imperfect verbal form expresses the psalmist’s confidence about the future. Another option is to take the form as expressing a prayer, “free me.”
Heb “my spirit.” The noun רוּחַ (ruakh, “spirit”) here refers to the animating spirit that gives the psalmist life.

verses.zh: 我恨恶那信奉虚无之神的人；我却倚靠耶和华。
verses.en: I hate those who serve worthless idols,[NOTE:1] but I trust in the Lord.
notes: Or “redeem.” The perfect verbal form is understood here as anticipatory, indicating rhetorically the psalmist’s certitude and confidence that God will intervene. The psalmist is so confident of God’s positive response to his prayer that he can describe his deliverance as if it had already happened. Another option is to take the perfect as precative, expressing a wish or request (“rescue me”; cf. NIV). See IBHS 494-95 §30.5.4c, d. However, not all grammarians are convinced that the perfect is used as a precative in biblical Hebrew.

verses.zh: 我要为你的慈爱高兴欢喜；因为你见过我的困苦，知道我心中的艰难。
verses.en: I will be happy and rejoice in your faithfulness,because you notice my painand you are aware of how distressed I am.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the ones who observe vain things of falsehood.” See Jonah 2:9.

verses.zh: 你未曾把我交在仇敌手里；你使我的脚站在宽阔之处。
verses.en: You do not deliver me over to the power of the enemy;you enable me to stand[NOTE:1] in a wide open place.
notes: Heb “you know the distresses of my life.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你怜恤我，因为我在急难之中；我的眼睛因忧愁而干瘪，连我的身心也不安舒。
verses.en: Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am in distress!My eyes grow dim[NOTE:1] from suffering.[NOTE:2] I have lost my strength.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “you cause my feet to stand.”
Or perhaps, “are swollen.”
Cf. Ps 6:7, which has a similar line.

verses.zh: 我的生命为愁苦所消耗；我的年岁为叹息所旷废。我的力量因我的罪孽衰败；我的骨头也枯干。
verses.en: For my life nears its end in pain;my years draw to a close as I groan.[NOTE:1] My strength fails me because of[NOTE:2] my sin,and my bones become brittle.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “my breath and my stomach [grow weak].” Apparently the verb in the previous line (“grow dim, be weakened”) is to be understood here. The Hebrew term נפשׁ can mean “life,” or, more specifically, “throat, breath.” The psalmist seems to be lamenting that his breathing is impaired because of the physical and emotional suffering he is forced to endure.
Heb “and my years in groaning.”
Heb “stumbles in.”

verses.zh: 我因一切敌人成了羞辱，在我的邻舍跟前更甚；那认识我的都惧怕我，在外头看见我的都躲避我。
verses.en: Because of all my enemies, people disdain me;[NOTE:1] my neighbors are appalled by my suffering[NOTE:2]—those who know me are horrified by my condition;[NOTE:3] those who see me in the street run away from me.
notes: Heb “grow weak.”
Heb “because of all my enemies I am a reproach.”

Heb “and to my neighbors, exceedingly.” If the MT is retained, then these words probably go with what precedes. However the syntactical awkwardness of the text suggests a revision may be needed. P. C. Craigie (Psalms 1-50 [WBC], 258) suggests that the initial mem (מ) on מְאֹד (meʾod, “exceedingly”) be understood as an enclitic mem (ם) which was originally suffixed to the preceding form and then later misinterpreted. The resulting form אֵד (ʾed) can then be taken as a defectively written form of אֵיד (ʾed, “calamity”). If one follows this emendation, then the text reads literally, “and to my neighbors [I am one who experiences] calamity.” The noun פַחַד (fakhad, “[object of] horror”) occurs in the next line; אֵיד and פַחַד appear in parallelism elsewhere (see Prov 1:26-27).

verses.zh: 我被人忘记，如同死人，无人记念；我好像破碎的器皿。
verses.en: I am forgotten, like a dead man no one thinks about;[NOTE:1] I am regarded as worthless, like a broken jar.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and [an object of ] horror to those known by me.”
Heb “I am forgotten, like a dead man, from [the] heart.” The “heart” is here viewed as the center of one’s thoughts.

verses.zh: 我听见了许多人的谗谤，四围都是惊吓；他们一同商议攻击我的时候，就图谋要害我的性命。
verses.en: For I hear what so many are saying,[NOTE:1] the terrifying news that comes from every direction.[NOTE:2] When they plot together against me,they figure out how they can take my life.
notes: Heb “I am like a broken jar.” One throws away a broken jar without a second thought because it is considered worthless and useless.
Heb “the report of many.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，我仍旧倚靠你；我说：你是我的　神。
verses.en: But I trust in you, O Lord!I declare, “You are my God!”

verses.zh: 我终身的事在你手中；求你救我脱离仇敌的手和那些逼迫我的人。
verses.en: You determine my destiny.[NOTE:1] Rescue me from the power of my enemies and those who chase me.
notes: Heb “the terror from all around.”

verses.zh: 求你使你的脸光照仆人，凭你的慈爱拯救我。
verses.en: Smile[NOTE:1] on your servant.Deliver me because of your faithfulness.
notes: Heb “in your hand [are] my times.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你叫我不致羞愧，因为我曾呼吁你；求你使恶人羞愧，使他们在阴间缄默无声。
verses.en: O Lord, do not let me be humiliated,for I call out to you.May evil men be humiliated.May they go wailing to the grave.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “cause your face to shine.”

verses.zh: 那撒谎的人逞骄傲轻慢，出狂妄的话攻击义人；愿他的嘴哑而无言。
verses.en: May lying lips be silenced—lips[NOTE:1] that speak defiantly against the innocent[NOTE:2] with arrogance and contempt.
notes: The verb יִדְּמוּ (yiddemu) is understood as a form of דָּמַם (damam, “wail, lament”). Another option is to take the verb from דָּמַם (“be quiet”; see BDB 198-99 s.v. I דָּמַם), in which case one might translate, “May they lie silent in the grave.”
Heb “the [ones which].”

verses.zh: 敬畏你、投靠你的人，你为他们所积存的，在世人面前所施行的恩惠是何等大呢！
verses.en: How great is your favor,[NOTE:1] which you store up for your loyal followers.[NOTE:2] In plain sight of everyone you bestow it on those who take shelter[NOTE:3] in you.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “godly.”
Or “How abundant are your blessings!”
Heb “for those who fear you.”

“Taking shelter” in the Lord is an idiom for seeking his protection. Seeking his protection presupposes and even demonstrates the subject’s loyalty to the Lord. In the psalms those who “take shelter” in the Lord are contrasted with the wicked and equated with those who love, fear, and serve the Lord (Pss 2:12; 5:11-12; 34:21-22).

verses.zh: 你必把他们藏在你面前的隐密处，免得遇见人的计谋；你必暗暗地保守他们在亭子里，免受口舌的争闹。
verses.en: You hide them with you, where they are safe from the attacks[NOTE:1] of men;[NOTE:2] you conceal them in a shelter, where they are safe from slanderous attacks.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “you work [your favor] for the ones seeking shelter in you before the sons of men.”
The noun רֹכֶס (rokhes) occurs only here. Its meaning is debated; some suggest “snare,” while others propose “slander” or “conspiracy.”
Heb “you hide them in the hiding place of your face from the attacks of man.” The imperfect verbal forms in this verse draw attention to God’s typical treatment of the faithful.

verses.zh: 耶和华是应当称颂的，因为他在坚固城里向我施展奇妙的慈爱。
verses.en: The Lord deserves praise[NOTE:1] for he demonstrated his amazing faithfulness to me when I was besieged by enemies.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “you conceal them in a shelter from the strife of tongues.”
Heb “blessed [be] the Lord.”

verses.zh: 至于我，我曾急促地说：我从你眼前被隔绝。然而，我呼求你的时候，你仍听我恳求的声音。
verses.en: I jumped to conclusions and said,[NOTE:1] “I am cut off from your presence!”[NOTE:2] But you heard my plea for mercy when I cried out to you for help.
notes: Heb “for he caused his faithfulness to be amazing to me in a besieged city.” The psalmist probably speaks figuratively here. He compares his crisis to being trapped in a besieged city, but the Lord answered his prayer for help. Verses 19-24 were apparently written after the Lord answered the prayer of vv. 1-18.
Heb “and I, I said in my haste.”

verses.zh: 耶和华的圣民哪，你们都要爱他！耶和华保护诚实人，足足报应行事骄傲的人。
verses.en: Love the Lord, all you faithful followers[NOTE:1] of his!The Lord protects those who have integrity,but he pays back in full the one who acts arrogantly.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “from before your eyes.”
A “faithful follower” (חָסִיד, khasid) is one who does what is right in God’s eyes and remains faithful to God (see Pss 4:3; 12:1; 16:10; 31:23; 37:28; 86:2; 97:10).

verses.zh: 凡仰望耶和华的人，你们都要壮胆，坚固你们的心！
verses.en: Be strong and confident,[NOTE:1] all you who wait on the Lord.
notes: The participial forms in the second and third lines characterize the Lord as one who typically protects the faithful and judges the proud.

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible
Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- There are so many Psalms where the author is seeking help from God against enemies. One wonders

- who are these enemies?

- why does the psalmist feel detached and attacked so often?

- were many of these written during the same period of the psalmist's life (probably David)?

- The psalmist faces several issues.

- personal sin and its mental and physical consequences (cf. Ps. 31:1-12)

- personal attacks by

- enemies

- neighbors

- acquaintances

- covenant partners

- family

- The actions of the enemies are characterized as

- trying to trap him in a net, Ps. 31:4

- trying to get him to regard idols, Ps. 31:6

- slandering him, Ps. 31:11,13,20

- counseling together against him, Ps. 31:13,20

- persecuting him, Ps. 31:15

- having lying lips, Ps. 31:18

- speaking arrogantly, Ps. 31:18

- Many/most of the Psalms in Book One have similar themes and wording. This may reflect
an unknown editing or compiling agenda. There was a purposeful structure to the different
books of Psalms (see Introduction to the Psalter, VI) but moderns are not sure what it was.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

31:1-5 Notice the very personal way the author addresses YHWH. Notice the number of personal
PRONOUNS. Biblical faith is a personal trust in a personal God. It is not initially
about a creed or even a moral code but about a personal encounter! That encounter changes everything!
All else is based on it.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHAT DOES IT MEAN TO "RECEIVE," "BELIEVE," "CONFESS/PROFESS," AND "CALL UPON"?

▣ This strophe has several prayer requests.

- Let me never be ashamed ‒ BDB 101, KB 116, Qal COHORTATIVE; this
shame could be connected to David's sin (cf. Psalm 32; 51) or others' attack on his reputation
or motives, cf. Ps. 25:2-3,20; 31:1,17; 35:26; 69:6; 119:6,46,78,80. Shame sometimes means
abandonment by YHWH (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 621-627).

- Deliver me ‒ BDB 812, KB 930, Piel IMPERATIVE

- Incline Your ear to me ‒ BDB 639, KB 692, Hiphil IMPERATIVE,
cf. Ps. 17:6; 71:2; 86:1; 88:2; 102:2

- Rescue me ‒ BDB 664, KB 717, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

- Be my rock ‒ BDB 224, KB 243, Qal IMPERATIVE

- Lead me ‒ BDB 634, KB 685, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Psalm 23

- Guide me ‒ BDB 624, KB 675, Hiphil IMPERFECT, cf. Psalm 23

- Pull me out of their net — BDB 422, KB 425, Hiphil IMPERFECT

His prayer requests are based on

- he has committed himself to YHWH, Ps. 31:5

- YHWH has ransomed him, Ps. 31:5 (see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM)

- YHWH is his strength, Ps. 31:4

- YHWH is the God of truth/faithfulness, Ps. 31:5 (see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT)

31:1 "refuge" This alludes to a strong hiding place of safety and security. See note
at Ps. 2:12.

spiritual Deity. The only vocabulary humans have is

- fallen

- physical

- cultural

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

▣ "rock" See note at Ps. 18:2. There are two different Hebrew words translated

- in Ps. 31:2 ‒ BDB 700

- in Ps. 31:3 ‒ BDB 849

- both refer to a place of stability, protection, and security (cf. Deut. 32:4,15,18,30)

31:3 "fortress" See note at Ps. 18:2.

▣ "For Your name's sake" See notes at Psalm 23:3 and 25:11. It represents
YHWH's character.

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

SPECIAL
TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD

31:3-4 Notice the series of IMPERFECTS that speak of continuous, ongoing actions.

- lead ‒ BDB 634, KB 685, Hiphil IMPERFECT

- guide ‒ BDB 624, KB 675, Piel IMPERFECT

- pull out ‒ BDB 422, KB 425, Hiphil IMPERFECT

31:4 "net" This was an instrument of hunting (BDB 440). It came to be used
figuratively of hurting or capturing humans (cf. Ps. 9:15; 10:9; 35:7-8; 57:6; 140:5). The psalmist's enemies
are secretly planning his destruction.

31:5 "into Your hand I commit my spirit" This was quoted by Jesus on the cross
just before His death (cf. Luke 23:46).

This VERB (BDB 823, KB 955, Hiphil IMPERFECT)
has a wide semantic field. Here it denotes an ongoing trust. This trust is based on who God is
(i.e., "God of truth," "faithful God"), not the merits of the psalmist.

▣ "hand" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND.

▣ "spirit" This is the Hebrew word ruah (BDB 924). Here it is the unseen
life force connected to YHWH breathing life into Adam in Gen. 2:7. When it leaves the body that body
goes to the holding place of the dead (Sheol).

31:6-8 This strophe is dominated by PERFECTS that denote a complete or
settled condition.

- I hate those who regard vain idols ‒ BDB 971, KB 1338, Qal PERFECT.
The intensity of the psalmist's requests for YHWH to judge is based on his worldview
(i.e., viewing the world as YHWH's agent). He hates those who break or ignore YHWH's covenant.
The LXX has "You hate." (i.e., Ps. 139:19-22)

- I trust in YHWH ‒ BDB 105, KB 120, Qal PERFECT; this is a
recurrent theme, cf. Ps. 4:5; 13:5; 25:2; 26:1; 28:7; 31:6,14; 52:8; 56:3,4,11; 91:2. If "fear
of YHWH is the beginning of knowledge" (cf. Prov. 1:7), then trust is the key to knowing Him personally.

- YHWH sees his affliction ‒ BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal PERFECT (cf. Exod. 3:7-8)

- YHWH knows his trouble ‒ BDB 393, KB 390, Qal PERFECT (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW)

- YHWH has not given him into the hands of his enemy ‒ BDB 688, KB 742, Hiphil
PERFECT

- YHWH has set his feet in a large place ‒ BDB 763, KB 840, Hiphil PERFECT,
cf. Ps. 18:19; 118:5; a large place is the opposite of a narrow place/strait, which is an idiom of
distress (cf. Ps. 4:1; 18:19; 118:5)

Stress (like sin, cf. Ps. 31:10c; Psalm 32, 51) causes physical manifestations.

31:19-22 This strophe describes YHWH's "goodness" (BDB 375, cf. Ps. 145:7). Probably
this strophe is to be understood after YHWH has answered the psalmist's prayer requests found early in
the psalm.

- It is stored up for those who fear YHWH.

- It is for those who take refuge in YHWH.

- YHWH hides His people

- in a secret place of His presence

- in a shelter/pavilion

- YHWH made His lovingkindness marvelous to the psalmist.

- YHWH heard his supplications.

31:19 "Before the sons of men" Not only does YHWH defend and protect, but He
acknowledges our special relationship to Him before our enemies (cf. Ps. 23:5).

▣ "fear" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT).

▣ "refuge" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE.

31:20 The secret place is the inner (or back) shrine of the temple/tabernacle (cf. Ps. 27:5). This
was a special place where the personal presence of YHWH was manifested (i.e., ark of the covenant).

31:21 "the Lord" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "lovingkindness" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS.

▣ "in a besieged city" Although we do not know the historical setting of this
Psalm, this phrase seems to be metaphorical. It describes a person who feels surrounded by wicked,
evil, lying people (i.e., "terror on every side," v. 13).

Even though the psalmist feels isolated, he believes YHWH hears and will act on his behalf.

The UBS Text Project (p. 213) gives this reading an "A" rating versus
"through distress," found in NEB.

The JPSOA translates this phrase as if it characterized why YHWH should be
"blessed," Ps. 31:21a. He is strong and unchanging (i.e., "a veritable bastion").
The Jewish Study Bible margin links this to YHWH as "a rock of strength," "a stronghold,"
"a crag" (i.e., rock), and "a fortress" in Ps. 31:2-3 (p. 1316).

31:22 "I am cut off from before Your eyes" The Jewish Study Bible (p. 1316) interprets
this phrase as meaning "absent from the temple" (i.e., 2 Chr. 26:21, where the same phrasing
is used of Uzziah being unable, as a leper, to go into the temple). The Niphal form of this
VERB (BDB 173, KB 202) is found only here in the OT.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why is the psalmist in such trouble?

- List the physical and social consequences of sin.

- Explain "shame" in an OT context.

- Is Ps. 31:21 literal or metaphorical?

- Why do so many Psalms written by an individual end in a corporate way?
